designRead.pageKind: form-flow — a fixed portrait self-service payment terminal, one decision per screen
designRead.audience: every driver at a Euro Parking site: any ability, any language, usually hurried, usually with a queue behind them, reading at arm's length in garage glare (BRIEF.md audience line; business-model.md driver story map, operator-reported and never observed — Q8/H19)
designRead.job: pay what this stay owes and get the card back in time to leave inside the fifteen-minute window
designRead.vibe: transport signage: flat bands, one face at four weights, nothing decorative, the deadline louder than the brand
designRead.systemFamily: named approximation of GOV.UK Design System (govuk-frontend) retuned to kiosk scale — plain language, one accent, ink-on-paper, focus made of a yellow bar and an ink keyline. Recorded as ADR-UI-001 in design-brief.md
designRead.signature: the black-on-signage-yellow WINDOW band that carries 'Leave by 11:22 · 14:32 left' — the one domain invariant (I1, ParkingVisit.md §3) a driver is judged by and today only finds out about at a closed barrier

dials.reason: variance 2 — the quiet constraints win (design-read.md signal 6): a public machine every driver must succeed at, in glare, at arm's length, with a queue; the audience picks the aesthetic and this audience picks convention. The only place boldness is spent is the yellow deadline band. motion 1 — a kiosk has no hover (prototype-craft.md), nothing may gate on a transition while someone waits behind you, the terminal must boot and run with the network down (TerminalOperations.md, partition tolerance), and the one thing that changes over time — the countdown — is information, not animation. density 2 — one question per screen: 67 minutes of stay, one amount, one action; the surface floor is 24px body and this design runs 28px because 'any ability' plus glare is more than the floor asks (prototype-craft.md § Surface floors).

iconography.family: none — text and drawn glyphs only (↓ → ✓ €); a terminal that must keep working with the network down ships no icon font, and every hardware target is labelled in words instead
